title: Gidel bar Re’ulai
author: Aharon Hyman

paragraphs: In Gittin 34a he sends a bill of divorce to his wife; he lived in the time of Abaye and Rava. There, 58b, he takes land from the district's residents on terms of paying its tax, and comes before Rav Papa. It is not known whether he was a Torah scholar.[^1][^2]

notes.text: ושם נח: means “and there, 58b,” not a man named Noah. The consulted passage names Giddul bar Re’ilai, tax arrangements and Rav Papa; Taska and Baga are not treated as two place names. The heading’s Re’ulai form remains.

The checked Gittin passages concern Giddul bar Re’ilai sending a bill of divorce and the tax and district-resident report to Rav Pappa. The supplied Re’ulai form and Hyman’s chronological account remain unchanged; no identification with Noah or conversion of the tax context into cities is supplied.
